learning: Iteration 4 has shown that the geometry is at its limit on s-bend and slalom, with one line loss per run and max_error near 0.065 m. Controller changes (kp, kd, base_speed, line-loss mode) remain untested, so the next step, if there were one, would be to test a single gain change against this baseline on the development tracks before racing it.
notes: Final complete robot: the Builder's iteration 4 geometry with the unchanged iteration 3 and 4 controller. Chosen because it is the best measured design, and an untested controller change would risk the unseen-track race in the last iteration.
rationale: The Builder holds the iteration 4 geometry unchanged: five sensors at +/-0.054 m in 0.027 m steps, sensor_size 0.012, mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.09, body 0.18 x 0.12, wheel radius 0.03. Iteration 4 is the best race so far (67.90). It cleared oval line losses (0.0 vs 0.6 at iteration 3) and lifted oval progress to 0.204, with oval max_error 0.0625 m. Its remaining faults are one line loss per run on s-bend (max_error 0.0669) and slalom (max_error 0.0648). Iterations 2 and 3 show that mass and wheel_track have already been tried on those bends without clearing them, so the geometry is at its range. Any controller change is untested, and this is the final iteration. Its design races unseen, so a risky change could take the score down from a known 67.9 level. The controller is therefore kept identical to iteration 4 (kp 4.0, ki 0.2, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.3, weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1], last_direction recovery). That keeps the robot working as measured on the development set. The observation request covers every measurement so the result can be read in full.
